span.span: You are given two simple undirected graphs FF and GG with nn vertices. FF has m1m_{1} edges while GG has m2m_{2} edges. You may perform one of the following two types of operations any number of times:
such that there is an edge between
such that there is no edge between

Determine the minimum number of operations required such taht for all integers uu and v⁡(1≤u,v≤n)v\ (1\leq u,v\leq n), there is a path from uu to vv in FF if and only if there is a path from uu to vv in GG.
Input
The first line contains an integer t⁡(1≤t≤104)t\ (1\leq t\leq 10^{4}) —the number of independent test cases.
The first line of each test case contains three integers n,m1n,m_{1} and m2(1≤n≤2⋅105,0≤m1,m2≤2⋅105)m_{2}\ (1\leq n\leq 2\cdot 10^{5},0\leq m_{1},m_{2}\leq 2\cdot 10^{5}) —the number of vertices, the number of edges in FF, and the number of edges in GG.
The following m1m_{1} lines each contain two integers uu and v⁡(1≤u,v≤n)v\ (1\leq u,v\leq n) —there is an edge between uu and vv in GG. It is guaranteed that there are no repeated edges or self loops.
It is guaranteed that the sum of nn, the sum of m1m_{1}, and the sum of m2m_{2} over all test cases do not exceed 2⋅1052\cdot 10^{5}.
Output
For each test case, output a single integer denoting the minimum operations required on a new line.
